note: The journalist's review of the claims in the evidence vault that are not in the site's claim table (data/claims.json). One row per reviewed claim: the verdict (used, agrees, held back), the reason, and the page it was reviewed for. A vault claim with no row here is shown on /claims/review/ as not yet reviewed, so a new export lists new claims without anyone editing a page.

verdicts.used: used on a page, attributed to its source
verdicts.agrees: agrees with a claim the site already carries; not repeated
verdicts.held back: not stated on the site as worded, for the reason given

reviews.reason: One Vietnamese outlet. Reuters, CNN and USA Today, in the vault, describe Prime Minister Takaichi urging website operators on X to check for PHP and prepare to patch, and, in CNN's account, saying companies should consider suspending services: a request, not an order.
TechTarget Japan gives 22 million (22.6 million in its headline) with no basis. The site's scale figures, each with what it measures, are on the numbers page.

Help Net Security does not say who confirmed it. What the vault holds is researchers demonstrating code execution against these applications (Calif; Wiz for WordPress and Drupal), which is not attackers succeeding against someone.

Unsourced. The earliest attempt in the record is Amazon's honeypot on 17 October 2026. A 2024 audit by Quarkslab found the out-of-memory issue without proving it exploitable, which may be where a 2024 date comes from.
Contradicts the confirmed discovery by Calif on 1 August and its report to PHP on 11 August. 20 October is the day of PHP's advance notice and of the leak.

SiliconANGLE's own description of the August work, which the site records as found by researchers using frontier AI under OpenAI's initiative (claim ai-found). Not used, so that it is not confused with the 2024 Quarkslab audit.
Agrees with the site's confirmed claim who-first (discovery 1 August, report to PHP 11 August).

'14 years' restates Wiz's lower bound, PHP 5.4 and later, as an age; it is one estimate restated, not an independent finding. Nobody in the vault names the commit that introduced the flaw. Which versions are affected is an explained contradiction on the fact-check desk.
As for '14 years': Wiz's PHP 5.4 bound, restated as a year.
Agrees with Wiz's own post ('dating back to PHP 5.4'). The CVE records list only the supported branches; see the site's disputed claim versions-old.
